correctness.rationale: Generator stationary characteristic product and independent exponential-Gaussian variance mixture are algebraically exact. R(y)=f(sqrt(2y))/phi(sqrt(2y)) is strictly convex, begins and ends above one and must fall below one, giving exactly two density crossings and one central-coverage crossing. Fourth moment and exponential concentration bound yield an L1 Taylor remainder O(s^(3/2)); Gaussian Hermite calculus gives sharp TV/K constants, and uniform CDF expansion gives crossover tending sqrt(3) with O(s^(1/2)) rate. Standalone VERIFY.py produced 62 checks, but analytic proofs bear all infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Exact stationary law and weak Gaussian convergence were established by Pierce 2022 and Tal-Friedman et al. 2022 and are explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Assefa et al. 2026 gives moment theory, not sharp probability metrics. The surviving distinct result is the unique sign-changing central interval radius for all contractions plus two sharp first-order metric constants in the weak-reset regime, which requires additional convex mixture comparison and uniform L1 work.

value.rationale: The all-contraction unique sign-switch determines whether Gaussian central coverage overstates or understates probability, and the limiting 91.673548% threshold is a meaningful calibration boundary. Sharp positive TV and Kolmogorov constants quantify exactly the error of the known Gaussian weak limit and cannot be read from its previously calculated moments alone. A natural statistical question for a canonical stochastic resetting model, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
